domains.title: Analog domain.
domains.subtitle: Shaping the future of VLSI.
description: Analog design in VLSI is the intricate process of developing circuits that process continuous signals, such as amplifiers, oscillators, and filters. These components are crucial for bridging digital and real-world interfaces.

Careful consideration of noise, power, and precision is at the core of analog VLSI design. The field evolves alongside advancements in technology, demanding expertise in both theory and practical implementation.

projects.title: Two Stage Cmos Opamp
projects.description: Operational amplifiers (Op-Amps) are fundamental building blocks in analog and mixed-signal circuit design, widely used in signal conditioning, filtering, data conversion, and many other applications. This project aims to design and analyse a two-stage CMOS operational amplifier tailored for general-purpose analog applications. The design emphasizes key performance parameters such as high open-loop gain, low power consumption, and sufficient output swing all essential for integration into modern VLSI systems.

domains.title: Computer Architecture domain.
domains.subtitle: Shaping the future of VLSI.
description: The Computer Architecture domain explores how software commands translate into physical action on a chip. It focuses on creating the processor's master blueprint, the essential bridge between code and hardware, to achieve maximum performance and efficiency.

Work in this domain begins with the fundamentals of Instruction Set Architectures (ISAs). From there, the core activity is designing and building a complete processor from the ground up. This is a hands-on process using industry-standard hardware description languages.

To create a truly high-performance processor, the domain covers the clever techniques that define modern computing. This includes implementing pipelining, sophisticated caching systems, and branch prediction.

projects.title: Floating Point Unit
projects.description: Architect and synthesize a Floating-Point Unit (FPU) in Verilog, the hardware core responsible for arithmetic with decimal numbers. This project covers the implementation of key operations like addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, with a focus on ensuring strict adherence to the IEEE 754 standard, the industry-wide protocol that governs modern floating-point computation.

projects.title: Arithmetic Logic Unit with Booth's Multiplier
projects.description: Design and synthesize the mathematical brain of a processor: an Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU) in Verilog. This project involves implementing a full range of standard arithmetic and logical operations. A special focus is placed on creating an optimized multiplication circuit using Booth's algorithm, a powerful technique for efficiently handling signed numbers while minimizing hardware resources.

domains.title: Simulation & Design domain.
domains.subtitle: Shaping the future of VLSI.
description: Simulation & Design focuses on the intricate process of creating and validating digital hardware designs. This involves designing circuits that operate on discrete binary signals (0s and 1s), which form the very backbone of modern electronics. These components are crucial for processing information in everything from mobile phones to high-performance computers.

Critical considerations of timing, power, and area (PPA) are at the core of every design. The field demands a strong foundation in logic synthesis and hardware description languages (HDLs), combined with practical expertise in physical implementation and verification.
